items.syntax: SELECT key, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY key
items.explanation: One output row per distinct key.
items.example: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customers DESC;

items.explanation: Both ignore NULLs. AVG of an integer column returns numeric in PostgreSQL.
items.example: SELECT category_id, SUM(units_in_stock) AS stock, ROUND(AVG(unit_price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY category_id;
items.expected: Stock and average price per category.

items.explanation: Work on numbers, dates and text.
items.example: SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_order, MAX(order_date) AS last_order FROM orders;
items.expected: One row with the first and last order date.

items.syntax: GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > n
items.explanation: HAVING filters after aggregation; WHERE filters rows before.
items.example: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY orders DESC;
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers FROM orders GROUP BY employee_id ORDER BY customers DESC;

items.explanation: PostgreSQL FILTER clause; portable form is SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).
items.example: SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE shipped_date IS NULL) AS unshipped, COUNT(*) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY employee_id;
items.expected: Unshipped and total orders per employee.

items.syntax: SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN x ELSE 0 END)
items.explanation: Several filtered totals in one pass.
items.example: SELECT ship_country, SUM(CASE WHEN freight > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS heavy, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY ship_country ORDER BY heavy DESC LIMIT 5;

items.explanation: Joins values into one string per group (PostgreSQL; MySQL uses GROUP_CONCAT).
items.example: SELECT category_id, STRING_AGG(product_name, ', ' ORDER BY product_name) AS products FROM products GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY category_id;
items.expected: One comma-separated product list per category.

items.explanation: Any expression can be a grouping key; repeat it or use the column position.
items.example: SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date)::date AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 6;
items.expected: Orders per month for the first 6 months.
